analysis: Examined the new Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.swift (head lines 1-567) for security-relevant behavior. Load path: the runtime requires an authenticated peer (`peerVerified`, line 141), establishes the keyed data plane with `tensorParallelSeal: true`, installs the seal codec, and checks the load-agreement and loaded-commitment digests between ranks (lines 157-189). It refuses non-native KV quantization and non-serial prefill, and rejects image/media inputs (reserve, line 356). `generate` compares the request fingerprint digest across ranks (line 494), so a rank given a different request fails closed. Errors in `start` call `control.fail()`, sweep the prefix cache, and withdraw the prefix capture, so the failure path does not leave plaintext-derived state reusable (lines 431-434, 522-525). Shutdown closes the disk tier and sweeps the cache. Logs carry request UUIDs, sizes and counts only, with no prompt or token content; the token chain is hashed. The prefix cache is the main new data-at-rest surface (T-041, A-001): the SSD tier is opened with an owner-supplied 32-byte key (`prefixSSDKey`), and nil disables it. Memory-pressure handling (lines 538-551) withdraws the capture and sheds entries. Not verifiable from the supplied evidence: `Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes/open/store`, so I could not confirm that cache scoping is account-bound (coordinator-authored cacheSalt) or that the sealed vote/confirmation is authenticated; `QwenStagePrefixDiskTier` key use, file naming (HMAC-keyed lookup tags) and TTL; and the Gemma4TensorParallelSelection.swift body, which has no visible text in this unit (only its metadata and a patch excerpt, with the file added). Integration should check that the cluster SSD prefix tier preserves T-041 posture: no raw prefix hashes on disk, per-account scope in the lookup tag, bounded TTL. No concrete regression was identified in the visible lines.
